articles.title: S Chand Launches PRISM, India's First Publisher-Led LMS, Putting Pedagogy Ahead of Technology
articles.content: S Chand announced the launch of S Chand PRISM, a state-of-the-art Learning Management System (LMS) designed to enhance teaching and learning experiences in schools. With this launch, S Chand becomes the first publishing house in India to offer its publishing and curriculum titles through an integrated LMS, bringing together traditional textbooks and digital learning on a single platform. As schools increasingly adopt digital tools to improve classroom engagement and learning outcomes, ensuring that technology remains aligned with curriculum requirements and effective teaching practices has become essential. Addressing this need, PRISM integrates S Chand’s trusted educational content with digital resources, classroom activities, assessments and analytics, creating a connected learning ecosystem for students, teachers, school administrators and parents. The platform offers several key features, including: Anytime, anywhere learning: Web and mobile access with online and offline functionality. Curriculum-aligned resources: S Chand’s educational content and digital learning materials on one platform. Collaborative learning: Tools encouraging student participation and classroom engagement. Multiple assessment formats: Helping teachers evaluate understanding and track progress. Data-driven analytics: Insights supporting informed decisions by teachers, administrators and parents. Mr Himanshu Gupta, Managing Director, S Chand Group, commented on the launch: “PRISM reflects the company’s belief in bringing print and digital together, with the printed book at the heart of learning. He emphasised that technology should serve how students learn, never dictate it.” Mr Jitendra Agnihotri, Chief Executive Officer, S Chand Publishing (School Education), added: “The platform is designed to extend the reach of strong teaching, not replace the teacher or the book. He added that PRISM lets the company reach learners through different media while retaining the rigour and trust associated with S Chand content.” The launch reinforces the importance of balancing technology with strong teaching practices. Reflecting this approach, PRISM prioritises curriculum quality and foundational learning while enabling students to access educational content through multiple formats. Just as a prism reveals different colours from a single beam of light, the platform offers multiple learning pathways while connecting the wider school community. Mr. Saurabh Mittal, Group Chief Financial Officer, S Chand Group, highlighted the strategic significance of the launch: “PRISM represents a long-term investment in school education and the company’s growth. By bringing content, assessment and analytics together, the platform aims to build lasting value for the school community and deepen the company’s relationships with the institutions it serves.” With PRISM, S Chand continues to bridge the gap between print and digital education, keeping teachers, textbooks and effective pedagogy at the centre of learning.

The iFresh sensor tracks ethylene levels every 10 seconds to detect early signs of over-ripening in fruits and vegetables. The Luxuriem range is available in 645L, 651L and 654L capacities, with prices starting at Rs 98,000. Vikhyat Rishi 27-Oct-2026 Whirlpool of India Limited has introduced its 6th Sense AI-powered Freshness Detection Technology in its recently launched Luxuriem range of 4-door refrigerators. The company claims it is India’s first technology of its kind, designed to detect early signs of over-ripening in fruits and vegetables, alerting consumers before the produce spoils and helping reduce food wastage. Survey ✅ Thank you for completing the survey! The technology aims to address a common problem in Indian households, where fruits and vegetables purchased in bulk are often forgotten in the refrigerator and end up going to waste. How Whirlpool’s Freshness Detection Technology works The technology uses Whirlpool’s proprietary iFresh Sensor Engine, which incorporates an iFresh Sensor built into the refrigerator’s crisper drawer. The sensor tracks ethylene, a naturally occurring gas released by fruits and vegetables as they ripen. The refrigerator scans the produce stored in the crisper drawer every 10 seconds and sends an alert when it detects an increase in ethylene levels associated with over-ripening. The technology is designed to account for varying ethylene emissions across different types of produce, including high-ethylene emitters such as apples, pears, kiwis, avocados and peaches, as well as low-ethylene emitters such as lettuce, cabbage, broccoli and cauliflower. The refrigerator also features a real-time user interface that displays the freshness status of the produce stored in the crisper drawer. AI learns from user feedback Whirlpool says the freshness detection system can adapt to how individual households manage their food. When an alert appears, users can inspect their produce and reset the notification. The system records this feedback and uses it to adjust future alert thresholds according to user preferences. The company describes the technology as an application of on-device AI designed to address an everyday household problem. However, the effectiveness of its freshness alerts and their ability to reduce food waste will depend on real-world performance across different types of produce and storage conditions. Whirlpool Luxuriem 4-door refrigerator: Price and availability The new technology expands Whirlpool’s premium Luxuriem 4-door refrigerator portfolio. The range will be available in capacities of 645 litres, 651 litres and 654 litres, with multiple premium finishes. Prices start at Rs 98,000 . The refrigerators will be available through leading retail stores and online platforms across India. Whirlpool has positioned the new technology as a way to make refrigerator storage more responsive by helping users keep track of produce that might otherwise remain unnoticed in the crisper...

articles.content: The Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur (IITKGP) has announced plans to set up India’s first dedicated academic school focused on Physical Artificial Intelligence (AI) with an investment worth Rs 35 crore. The school will be named 'Benjamin Gupta School of Physical AI'. This new school will be laid under a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed by IIT Kharagpur, its alumnus and philanthropist Vinod Gupta, and the IITKGP Foundation USA. This project will receive a contribution of Rs 12.5 crore from alumnus Vinod Gupta's family and Rs 10 crore from an anonymous alumnus, while IIT Kharagpur will provide the remaining funds. The institute added that the new school will work in areas such as physics-informed machine learning, scientific AI, digital twins, intelligent robotics, autonomous systems, advanced sensing and AI-based experimentation. AI The school will also focus on developing AI systems that are reliable, explainable and responsible, particularly for applications where accuracy and safety are important. Academic programmes in this school are expected to begin from the upcoming academic session, subject to the necessary approvals. The proposed programmes will cater to students, researchers and working professionals from engineering, physical sciences, life sciences and medicine, with a special focus on combining domain knowledge with modern AI skills. Unlike conventional AI, which primarily focuses on data, algorithms and digital systems, this Physical AI school will aim to develop intelligent systems capable of understanding and interacting with the physical world. It integrates AI with scientific principles, real-world sensing and intelligent control, IIT Kharagpur stated in an official statement. The school will also partner with industry, healthcare institutions, research laboratories, startups and international partners to promote research, technology development and professional reskilling in Physical AI, the official statement said. IIT Kharagpur Director Suman Chakraborty said the school aims to take AI beyond its role as a “black-box” technology by combining algorithmic capabilities with fundamental scientific and domain-specific knowledge. articles.title: Bengaluru's Rs 6,000 Crore Elevated Railway Terminal Likely To Get DPR From Aarvee Associates
articles.content: Oct 27, 2026 | Updated 01:47 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Hyderabad-based Aarvee Associates is likely to prepare the detailed project report (DPR) for India’s first fully elevated railway coaching terminal proposed at Yelahanka in north Bengaluru, Money Control reported . South Western Railway (SWR) is expected to award the engineering consultancy firm a Rs 3.2 crore contract after two rounds of tendering failed to produce a successful bidder, according to a source in SWR’s Construction Organisation. The contract will be awarded by modifying an existing agreement for Final Location Survey work. Such modifications allow additional assignments linked to newly sanctioned projects to be given to an existing consultant. The consultancy will cover site investigations, master planning, urban design, engineering and preparation of the DPR for the proposed Yelahanka Mega Coaching Terminal. The project also includes expanding coaching maintenance and platform facilities at the Rail Wheel Factory (RWF) in Yelahanka. SWR initially cancelled the tendering process after identifying missing annexures in the documents. The tender was subsequently issued again, but both participating firms, Prime Rail and Nagpur-based Axykno, were disqualified. The railway zone then opted to assign the work to Aarvee Associates under the variation provision of an existing contract. Abhay Kumar Gupta, Chief Administrative Officer (Construction) at SWR, and Manjunath Kanamadi, the zone’s Chief Public Relations Officer, were unavailable for comment. The proposed terminal is estimated to cost Rs 6,000 crore and is planned across 20 acres. It could be developed through a public-private partnership (PPP) or a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) model. The facility is expected to have 16 platforms, significantly increasing capacity compared with the existing Yelahanka station, which has five platforms. The proposed site includes around 15 acres from the Rail Wheel Factory’s 192 acres land parcel and approximately two acres of private land, besides the existing station yard and RWF staff quarters. articles.title: Maharashtra becomes first state to deploy eight drug quality detector machines - Mid-Day
articles.content: Home / Mumbai / Mumbai News / Article / Maharashtra government introduces Rs 1.2 crore machines to check medicine quality Maharashtra government introduces Rs 1.2 crore machines to check medicine quality Updated On: 27 October, 2026 08:40 AM IST | Mumbai | Ritika Gondhalekar Maharashtra becomes first in India to use the technology in public health sector; all medicines procured by government to be tested Listen to this article : State Health Minister Prakashrao Abitkar displays one of the machines on Monday. PIC/RITIKA GONDHALEKAR In a move aimed at strengthening medicine quality checks in the public healthcare system , the Maharashtra government has procured eight drug quality detector machines, becoming the first state in India to adopt the technology, which is already being used in around 50 countries. One machine per region As of now, one machine has been allocated to each region, with the equipment expected to improve the monitoring of medicines supplied to government-run healthcare facilities. “A flying squad of two officials for each region has been established to conduct tests and send adulterated samples to NABL (National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories) for further testing. Medicines found to be suitable as per prescribed criteria will have a ‘passed’ indication, while any error will be marked with a ‘failed’ indication. Action will be initiated against manufacturers and sellers accordingly,” said Abitkar, while addressing the media at Arogya Bhavan on Monday. While the prestigious Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) have already integrated artificial intelligence (AI) into their programmes, several private B-schools are also updating their curricula and offering AI-related courses to students. According to Tapan Kumar Nayak, director of Jaipuria School of Business, generative AI has made the core promise of management education -- developing good judgement under uncertainty -- more difficult to deliver. "We have designed a dedicated 30-hour course on 'Emerging Technologies and AI for Business Leaders' in the first-year curriculum. Some of the best B-Schools teach a compulsory 2-3 month course on 'AI Foundations for Managers'. articles.title: IIT-Kharagpur Establishes India's First Physical AI School - Rediff.com
articles.content: IIT-Kharagpur is set to revolutionise AI education in India by establishing the Benjamin Gupta School of Physical AI, the nation's first dedicated academic institution focused on intelligent systems interacting with the physical world. IIT-Kharagpur on Monday said it will establish India's first dedicated academic school focused on Physical Artificial Intelligence (AI), with an investment of Rs 35 crore. The Benjamin Gupta School of Physical AI will be set up under a memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed by IIT-Kharagpur, its distinguished alumnus and philanthropist Vinod Gupta, and the IITKGP Foundation USA, according to an institute statement. The initiative will receive Rs 12.5 crore from the Vinod Gupta family, Rs 10 crore from an anonymous alumnus, with the institute funding the remaining amount. Named in memory of Gupta's late son, Benjamin Gupta, the school will house the Department of Artificial Intelligence and support interdisciplinary academic and research activities, a statement said. Unlike conventional AI, which primarily relies on data, algorithms and digital applications, Physical AI focuses on developing intelligent systems that can understand and interact with the physical world by incorporating scientific principles, real-world sensing and intelligent control, it said. The school will focus on areas such as physics-informed machine learning, scientific AI, digital twins, intelligent robotics, autonomous systems, advanced sensing and AI-enabled experimentation, it added. It aims to develop reliable, explainable and responsible AI technologies, particularly for safety-critical applications where physical accuracy, robustness and accountability are essential, the statement said. Academic programmes are expected to begin in the upcoming session, subject to necessary approvals. They will cater to students, researchers and working professionals from engineering, physical sciences, life sciences and medicine, with an emphasis on combining domain expertise with contemporary AI capabilities. "AI has transformed the way we process information. Its next great leap will be in transforming the way we understand, engineer and interact with the physical world. IIT-Kharagpur aspires to lead this transition in India through the Benjamin Gupta School of Physical AI," institute director Suman Chakraborty said. He said the initiative would seek to move beyond treating AI as a black-box solution and encourage professionals to combine algorithmic capabilities with fundamental scientific and domain-specific knowledge. The school will bring together academia, industry, healthcare institutions, research laboratories, startups and international partners to accelerate research, technology development and professional reskilling, the statement added. articles.title: IIT Kharagpur AI School to Focus on Physical AI - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News IIT Kharagpur’s AI School Targets India’s Physical Systems Push Breaking News IIT Kharagpur’s AI School Targets India’s Physical Systems Push By Tenzin Choden October 27, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp IIT Kharagpur has signed a tripartite memorandum of understanding with alumnus and philanthropist Vinod Gupta and the IIT Kharagpur Foundation, US, to establish India’s first dedicated AI school, an institution aimed at applying artificial intelligence to physical systems and engineering challenges. The Benjamin Gupta School of Physical AI will receive an estimated Rs 35 crore in funding. The Vinod Gupta family will contribute Rs 12.5 crore, another alumnus will provide Rs 10 crore, and IIT Kharagpur will fund the remaining amount. The money will support dedicated infrastructure for the institute’s artificial intelligence department and related interdisciplinary academic and research activities. According to IIT Kharagpur, the school will focus on moving AI beyond data-driven algorithms and digital applications towards systems that can understand, predict and interact with the physical world. Its work will combine artificial intelligence with engineering, science, medicine, biological systems and real-world technologies. The proposed research areas include physics-informed machine learning, scientific AI, digital twins, intelligent robotics, autonomous systems, advanced sensing, computational engineering and AI-enabled experimentation. These areas are closely linked to how physical infrastructure and industrial systems are designed, monitored and operated. The institute said the school’s research is expected to address advanced manufacturing, energy, climate and environmental technologies, agriculture, healthcare, medical devices, infrastructure and next-generation engineering systems. The focus places the institution within a growing effort to connect AI research with sectors where software must interact with machinery, materials, buildings, energy networks and other physical environments. IIT Kharagpur director Suman Chakraborty said the next major advance in AI would involve changing how humans understand, engineer and interact with the physical world. He said the school would help India move from being a user of AI technologies to becoming a creator of intelligent physical systems. Academic programmes are expected to begin from the upcoming academic session, subject to approvals. The proposed offerings include hybrid master’s programmes, executive education, professional certification courses and specialised interdisciplinary modules for students, researchers, working professionals, engineers, scientists and medical graduates. The school has been named after Benjamin Gupta, Vinod Gupta’s late son, who died at the age of 28. Benjamin was pursuing a joint JD/MBA programme at The George Washington University and had been associated with former US Representative Rahm Emanuel and the US Department of State. Gupta, a Life Fellow of IIT Kharagpur, said the initiative was personally meaningful because it honours his son’s memory. The immediate next step is the development of the school’s dedicated infrastructure and academic programmes, subject to the required approvals before the proposed courses can begin.
